linkedin.title: Most people are tired of the news, and I understand why.
linkedin.body:
It feels like we are constantly drinking from a firehose. Every morning brings a flood of headlines, notifications, and breaking alerts that compete for our attention but rarely add much to our understanding of the world.

We have confused volume with value. Staying informed should not mean reading everything. It should mean reading the right things for you. When you try to keep up with absolutely everything, you end up knowing a little bit about a lot of topics, but rarely enough to form a real opinion.

Personalization is the solution, but not in the way social media algorithms use it. We do not need echo chambers that just show us what we already agree with. We need tools that filter out the noise so we can engage deeply with the stories that actually impact our lives, our work, and our interests.

When you strip away the sensationalism and the endless scrolling, you are left with the information that actually matters. That is how we stay genuinely informed without burning out.

slides.explanation: The vessel was not stationed in Libya. It had stopped at the port only for fuel and supplies on its journey back to Russia when the explosion occurred.
